summary: Real browser Linux compiled original and edited Go, executed Go tests and channels, and saved/reopened database records. Upload guards and source/database archive recovery passed separate real-VM checks. This remains a runtime prototype: the first published-site build took about seven minutes on this desktop.
environment: Chromium desktop, real externally hosted JSLinux x86-64 with a Go-equipped BusyBox/musl root, 768 MiB configured guest RAM

verification_scope.compilation: Original and edited source compiled from published GitHub Pages assets.
verification_scope.tests_and_patterns: Actual Go tools executed in the hosted emulator with a local mirror of course-owned image files.
verification_scope.recovery: Recovery-only check uses an uploaded native-compiled Go reference binary to isolate transfer and persistence from compilation. Compiler execution is verified separately.
verification_scope.journey: The initial full journey passed Go checks but exposed a Stop interaction after export. Stop was moved beside the terminal; guarded transfer and fresh-session restore were then exercised separately.

limits: These are functional feasibility checks, not evidence of learning effectiveness.
Times are observed desktop waits with a prepared build cache, not controlled language benchmarks.
Physical Android/tablet performance and file-picker behavior remain unverified.
The externally hosted runtime is not a complete offline installation.
A direct Go compiler/linker WASI probe ran in Node, but browser integration for that route remains unverified.
